newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia May coffee output up 12.21 pct over '96. [CORRECTED 23:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Colombia May coffee output up 12.21 pct over '96. [CORRECTED 23:45 GMT]

text.p: Colombia's produced 836,000 60-kg bags of coffee in May, up a surprising 12.21 percent over the 745,000 bags produced during the same month last year, sources at the National Coffee Growers' Federation said Wednesday.

The sources said production from October 1995 through May 1996 totalled just 7.29 million bags, however, down from 9.9 million in October 1995 through May 1996. (Corrects from "down from 9.9 million in October 1995 through May 1997")

Private exporters, wo have been complaining for weeks about what they describe as extremely tight supplies of fresh green coffee in Colombia, said the May production figure was sharply higher than expected and was sure to surprise the market. "The figure seems awfully high to me," a trader said. "I haven't seen that much coffee around," he added, saying his own estimates had put production at no more than about 500,000 bags. John Naranjo, production manager at the National Coffee Growers' Federation, told Reuters in an interview Tuesday that production was expected to total no more than about 10 million bags during the current coffe year. "That's very little," he said.
